newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies higher.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb higher while pork belly futures were called 0.200 to 0.500 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Analysts anticipate a steady to instances higher cash hog trend Friday which prompted ideas of steady to higher futures. Carryover demand from Thursday's rally and higher pork cutout values were also expected to prompt early demand in futures, they said.
Many pork plants will be closed Saturday and Monday but packers are still looking for hogs, sources said.
Japan's announcement it will exempt some pork imports from tariffs during August remains an underlying supportive factor, they added.

One Japanese supermarket chain said it will cut retail prices of imported pork by up to 15 percent during August to match the government's decision to exempt some pork imports from tariffs and in order to lower prices for consumers.

Pork bellies were seen higher on carryover demand from the limit advance in August and sharp gains in other months on Thursday. Firm cash belly prices and reduced hog kills remain supportive, analysts said.
